summary: Elderly man with high-grade unclassified sarcoma (malignant fibrous histiocytoma) of the right femur, now widely metastatic (lung, pelvic nodes, cerebellum), off anticoagulation with IVC filter, transferred from an outside hospital after a mechanical fall at home. Outside head CT showed intracranial bleeding which neurosurgery attributed to hemorrhage within his known cerebellar metastasis rather than trauma; he was asymptomatic neurologically and underwent planned CyberKnife radiosurgery to the brain metastasis during the stay. Labs show severe hypoproliferative anemia (Hgb 7.7), thrombocytopenia (Plt 63), leukocytosis (WBC 16.1), and imaging shows progressive pulmonary metastases; care goals are palliative with planned hospice transition.
most_likely: Hemorrhage into cerebellar metastasis from metastatic high-grade sarcoma (secondary malignant neoplasm of brain)

differential.diagnosis: Secondary malignant neoplasm of brain (cerebellar metastasis) with intratumoral hemorrhage
supporting_evidence: "bleeding is in the known metastatic lesion he has"
Prior MRI: 12 x 8 mm right cerebellar enhancing lesion
Received CyberKnife to brain met this admission
differential.reasoning: The condition that drove admission, neurosurgical evaluation and definitive treatment (CK radiosurgery) this stay is the hemorrhagic cerebellar metastasis, making it the principal disease for coding.

differential.diagnosis: Metastatic high-grade unclassified sarcoma of right femur with pulmonary metastases
supporting_evidence: CXR: multiple bilateral nodules, advanced metastatic disease
CT C-spine: new 1.4 cm right apical lung nodule, worsening metastasis
Prior path: recurrent high-grade sarcoma, iliac node biopsy positive
opposing_evidence: No new tumor-directed systemic therapy given
differential.reasoning: Underlying malignancy is actively progressing and drives every current problem; strongly codable as the underlying/secondary neoplastic diagnosis.

differential.diagnosis: Severe hypoproliferative anemia due to chronic thigh hematoma and malignancy
supporting_evidence: Hgb 7.7, Hct 23.6, MCV 101, RDW 20
Plan: maintain Hgb >7, weekly transfusions for palliation
Prior admissions for Hgb 4–5 from thigh hematoma
opposing_evidence: No active extravasation on prior CTA
differential.reasoning: Ongoing transfusion-dependent anemia is actively managed this stay and clearly documented, warranting a high secondary rank.

supporting_evidence: OSH head CT with intracranial bleeding
Neurosurgery felt bleed unrelated to the fall
Thrombocytopenia Plt 63 and chronically elevated INR
opposing_evidence: Small volume, no neurologic deficit, no intervention
differential.reasoning: A discrete, documented hemorrhagic event codable alongside the metastasis; scored below the metastasis because it is attributed to the tumor rather than an independent stroke.

supporting_evidence: Platelet count 63 K/uL
Note: "Elevated INR # Thrombocytopenia", goal Plt >50k
Prior acquired coagulation factor deficiency coded
opposing_evidence: No current INR value in structured labs
differential.reasoning: Documented and monitored this admission, contributing to bleeding risk and precluding anticoagulation.

supporting_evidence: Exam: enlarged girth of R proximal thigh, firm laterally

Prior CT: 15.7 x 14.5 x 30.3 cm mass/hematoma
opposing_evidence: Nontender, no acute bleeding this stay
differential.reasoning: Chronic ongoing problem addressed in the current plan as the source of transfusion-dependent blood loss.

differential.diagnosis: Mechanical fall due to weakness and non-weight-bearing right leg
supporting_evidence: "got up this morning to use the bathroom and fell over"
Attributes fall to weakness; uses crutches/wheelchair
Contusion left forehead, knee and elbow abrasions
opposing_evidence: No syncope or loss of consciousness
differential.reasoning: The admission mechanism and a codable external cause/symptom, but not a principal disease; deconditioning and functional loss explain it.

differential.diagnosis: Encounter for palliative care / hospice transition in terminal malignancy
supporting_evidence: DNR/DNI code status documented
Planned transition to hospice, transfusions for palliation
No further tumor-directed therapy options
opposing_evidence: Formal hospice enrollment deferred to patient readiness
differential.reasoning: Explicit goals-of-care/palliative status documented, commonly coded as an additional status diagnosis for this stay.

differential.diagnosis: Leukocytosis of uncertain etiology in advanced malignancy
supporting_evidence: WBC 16.1 K/uL
History of back abscess/cellulitis and prior unexplained fevers
opposing_evidence: Afebrile T 97.5, CXR no consolidation, benign urinalysis
differential.reasoning: Isolated leukocytosis without infectious source; likely tumor- or stress-related, so low score but worth noting.

differential.diagnosis: Chronic pulmonary embolism with IVC filter, anticoagulation contraindicated
supporting_evidence: Note: "Extensive B/L PE and DVT... IVC filter"
DVT prophylaxis contraindicated due to bleeding diathesis
opposing_evidence: No dyspnea, hypoxia or new imaging of PE this stay
differential.reasoning: Chronic comorbidity influencing management decisions but not an active problem driving this admission.

rule_outs.diagnosis: Traumatic intracranial hemorrhage / subdural hematoma from fall

CT C-spine showed no fracture or traumatic malalignment.

rule_outs.diagnosis: Pneumonia / sepsis explaining leukocytosis and fall
rule_outs.why: Afebrile, CXR without consolidation, bland urinalysis.

rule_outs.diagnosis: Acute blood loss anemia from active thigh bleeding
